answer: Sybils can be exposed with silent nudge tests. Each epoch the network secretly delays pay to one random seat, recorded in a sealed onyx log that opens only after close, so outsiders can't see it. An independent agent has no reason to react to a stranger's delay; an operator steering a farm notices its own shortfall and shifts jobs or effort across its seats. Seats whose output moves within hours of a nudge to another seat get linked, like a comet trail pointing back to one source, and linked seats share one reward. The log later serves as a lantern so anyone can audit the links.
